p1: For 17 years, the FBI hunted a bomber... and the man who stopped him was his own brother.
1978. A bomb at a Chicago university.
Then more. Universities... airlines. The FBI code-named him UNABOM.
Then, in 1995, he made an offer.
Publish his 35,000-word manifesto... and the bombings would stop.
The New York Times and The Washington Post printed it.
In New York, a man named David read it... and recognized his brother's writing.
April 1996. Agents surrounded a tiny cabin in Montana. No electricity. No running water.
Inside: 40,000 pages of journals... and one live bomb. Ready to mail.
That bomb never left the cabin... because his brother spoke up.
